Dear Olga and Meena,

I have done a label-free SRM experiment and quantified 97 proteins across 18 different samples. During the data-analyzation I have come across with many puzzling issues, which I am about to tell to you –quite extensively! I’m sorry I haven’t separated the issues to different topics to maybe make more sense.

One of the problems I have faced is the error message “input string is not in the correct format” in using the group comparison tool –this problem is sometimes overcome by changing the computer, but I still feel it’s quite strange thing to happen. Do you know what I should do in order to overcome this problem altogether?

Currently my biggest problem concerns the use of MSstats (2.3.4) group comparison tool and “allow missing peaks” option. Although I have checked the box, the log file shows FALSE in fill incomplete rows. Therefore the MSstats “couldn’t finish analysis” I guess? Is there a way to overcome this problem? See attachments.


Moreover, I have been wondering if it is possible to include only duplicates into the assay where in other conditions/strains there have been biological triplicates? The exclusion of the third biological replicate is usually done because of ion enhancement or suppression of a particular peptide in one of the samples(/replicates). I think what happens now is that the remaining duplicates representing the peptide under certain condition are also excluded, and the protein is quantified based on only the other peptides representing the target protein. Question is if there is a way to include this peptide still to the analysis with only two biological replicates?

 

Then I have a more general question about the normalization method for my data. Since I have done a label-free SRM with 97 protein targets, is that usually considered as large protein amount? If so, do you recommend quantile normalization over equalize medians -normalization? The majority of the proteins do not change so much, as I have seen from the testing results –file obtained from analysis made with either equalize medians or quantile normalization (with earlier functioning versions of MSstats group comparison-tool). Or should I use the “relative to global standards” –where I could use a few peptides which have been targeted in all inclusion lists and have similar signal intensities across all samples? Could you please tell me what are my options or what you would recommend?

 

Couple of questions still… bear with me!

 

In many of the group comparisons I have made with either equalize medians or with quantile normalization, I have gotten quite many zero p-values (10-40% of the 97 protein targets, depending on the comparison). Is this normal/typical/possible?! The results seem reliable, ie. the trends of up or down-regulation for each of the peptides representing these zero p-value proteins seem consistent. I found in MSstats 2.1.6-1 manual the similar situation in the example data to support that p-values actually can be zero, but I’m doubting still... What do you think? I can send you the files, but maybe rather as a private mail.

parts:
Dear Linda,

1. 'Input string is not in the correct format' error : I'm not clear why with only this error message. If you could send me .log file with this computer, or any screen capture and so on, will be helpful for me to know why. But, if it didn't happen in other computer, I think the problem is not about MSstats package itself. probably, window setting or R.. This is my guess.

2. Thank you for letting me know this issue. I fixed all the issues related in 'group comparison' function. Please check the post, "MSstats external tool in Skyline v2.3.4 re-updated on Oct 14"

3. I'm not sure whether I understood correctly or not. Could you make the design of experiment first? It seem 6 condition * 3 biological replicates * 3 technical replicates = total 54 MS runs. and it seems fractionation. is it correct? I tried to draw the profile plot, and I couldn't find the case you mentioned. Could you explain with some specific case?

4. normalization for label-free SRM : I generally do not recommend equalize median or quantile normalization for label-free SRM. When I say 'large' number of proteins, I generally means several thousands. Less than 100 proteins is not large number for me, even though you expect few of them to change. So, I recommend use global standards with protein or peptides that you know that they should be equal amount across all samples or that you already spike-in the same amount during sample processing step. and I just found that data seems fractionation. in this case, there are less number of peptides per run. so, equalize median and quantile normalization shouldn't be used.

5. p-value : first zero p-value in result is not actually zero, but very very small value, really close to zero. and There is no answer for how many or what proportion of proteins are significant. It really depends on your experiment. If you already checked the profile plot and result together, and it seems reliable, I think that it is not huge problem for analysis. However, just one comment, I don't know how many peptide per protein and how many transitions per peptide you used and how profile plot looks like or how the quality of data is. If you have quite large number of them in a proteins and there is not much variation across features, p-values could be less. If features are quite parallel across condition, you can use 'interference=FALSE" in groupComparison function in R or uncheck 'Include interference transition' in MSstats Group Comparison window in external tool.

6.  installation issue : This error message from generated in Skyline itself is not helpful for me. Have you checked 'Known issue. pdf' file in MSstats external webpage under Skyline? (https://skyline.gs.washington.edu/labkey/skyts/home/software/Skyline/tools/details.view?name=MSstats)? I suspected that there is any administrator authority problem. If you still have the problem to check 'Known issue' file, please let me know with more details(screenshot when it stop..)

Hope to be helpful for you.

messages.author: 701dadf5d5bd3f3b
messages.subject: Re: MSstats installation and group comparison -tool issues, questions about replicates and normalization etc...
parts:
Dear Linda,

From the description, it appears that your input data file is still structured incorrectly.

Your key comment was that, for each of the 2 groups and 3 biological replicates per group, the peptides were targeted in 3 different transition lists. The different transition lists are called 'methods' in the language of Skyline and MSstats, and are very important. Essentially, MSsats needs to know that each transition list was acquired separately. 

Currently MSstats mistakes multiple methods for repeated measurements of a same biological replicate under multiple conditions (hence the message 'time course'). Since not every method is acquired in every condition, MSstats thinks that there are many missing values. The profile plots therefore do not produce lines. And MSstats attempts to fill in the missing values according to its interpretation of the design. This is incorrect. Please see bullet (i) on page 8 of the user manual for a description of how to set up different methods. A correct setup will produce profile plots with lines.

Regarding the scope of biological replication: it is determined with respect to the number of biological replicates, not with respect to the number of proteins. Since you have only 3 biological replicates per group, reduced scope of biological replication is appropriate. However keep in mind that you will likely have many false positive differences. Expanded scope of biological replication always results in more conservative (but more reproducible) results. However it typically requires a larger number of biological replicate than what you have.

HTH
Olga
